format: Text with inline TeX in $...$ and display TeX in $$...$$. Answer label and value fields are TeX without delimiters.

problems.title: A linearly polarized wave
problems.prompt: Describe the polarization of $\mathbf{E}=\hat{\mathbf{x}}\,3\cos(\omega t-kz)+\hat{\mathbf{y}}\,4\cos(\omega t-kz)\ \mathrm{V/m}$, and find its amplitude and the angle of $\mathbf{E}$ from the $x$ axis.
hints: Both components have the same phase, so $\delta=0$.
steps: $\delta=0$, so the wave is linearly polarized.

problems.title: Which way does it turn?
problems.prompt: Find the polarization state of $\mathbf{E}=\hat{\mathbf{x}}\,5\cos(\omega t-kz)-\hat{\mathbf{y}}\,5\sin(\omega t-kz)\ \mathrm{V/m}$.
hints: Write $-\sin\theta$ as a cosine with a phase shift.
Then read off $\delta$ and use the sign rule.
steps: $a_x=a_y=5$ and $\delta=+90^\circ$, so the wave is left-hand circularly polarized.

Check at $z=0$: $\omega t=0$ gives $\mathbf{E}=5\hat{\mathbf{x}}$; $\omega t=90^\circ$ gives $\mathbf{E}=-5\hat{\mathbf{y}}$. Looking at the wave coming toward you, $\mathbf{E}$ turns clockwise, which is the left-hand rule about $+\hat{\mathbf{z}}$.

problems.title: From a phasor to the time domain
problems.prompt: A wave in air has $\tilde{\mathbf{E}}=10(\hat{\mathbf{x}}-j\hat{\mathbf{y}})e^{-jkz}\ \mathrm{V/m}$. Write $\mathbf{E}(z,t)$ and name its polarization.

problems.title: Characterizing an ellipse
problems.prompt: Find $\psi_0$, the rotation angle $\gamma$, the ellipticity angle $\chi$, the axial ratio and the handedness of $\tilde{\mathbf{E}}=(\hat{\mathbf{x}}\,3+\hat{\mathbf{y}}\,4e^{j45^\circ})e^{-jkz}$.
hints: $\tan2\psi_0$ is negative here, but $\cos\delta>0$ means $\gamma>0$: take the angle in the right quadrant.
steps: $\chi>0$, so the wave is left-hand elliptically polarized.

problems.title: Equal amplitudes, not circular
problems.prompt: Characterize $\tilde{\mathbf{E}}=2(\hat{\mathbf{x}}+\hat{\mathbf{y}}e^{-j60^\circ})e^{-jkz}$: find $\gamma$, $\chi$, the axial ratio and the handedness.
steps: $\psi_0=45^\circ$ and $\cos\delta>0$, so the major axis lies at $\gamma=45^\circ$.
$\chi<0$: right-hand elliptical. Equal amplitudes give a circle only when $\delta=\pm90^\circ$.

problems.title: Two circular waves make a line
problems.prompt: An LHC wave $\tilde{\mathbf{E}}_1=a(\hat{\mathbf{x}}+j\hat{\mathbf{y}})e^{-jkz}$ and an RHC wave $\tilde{\mathbf{E}}_2=a(\hat{\mathbf{x}}-j\hat{\mathbf{y}})e^{-jkz}$ travel together. Find the polarization of their sum. What if the RHC wave is $a(\hat{\mathbf{x}}-j\hat{\mathbf{y}})e^{j60^\circ}e^{-jkz}$ instead?
hints: Add the phasors component by component.
With the extra phase, factor out $e^{j30^\circ}$ and look at what is left.
steps: Still linear, but tilted to $30^\circ$: shifting the phase of one circular wave by $\phi$ rotates the line by $\phi/2$.

problems.title: Working backward from the ellipse
problems.prompt: A right-hand elliptically polarized wave toward $+z$ has axial ratio 3 and its major axis at $\gamma=30^\circ$ from the $x$ axis. Find $\psi_0$ and $\delta$.
steps: Check: $\delta$ is negative (right-handed) and $\cos\delta>0$ (so $\gamma>0$), as required.

problems.title: A phase over 90 degrees
problems.prompt: Characterize $\mathbf{E}=\hat{\mathbf{x}}\cos(\omega t-kz)+\hat{\mathbf{y}}\,2\cos(\omega t-kz+135^\circ)$: find $\gamma$, $\chi$, the axial ratio and the handedness.
